covered: Delayed lifecycle completion beyond the former 30-second browser deadline, exact-request deduplication, conflicting legacy/new submissions, and independent participant admission
GET-only reconciliation after lost acceptance, definitive rejection versus unconfirmed partial changes, missing receipts, dismissal without replay, delayed-response fencing and access loss

findingsAddressed: Individual Stop no longer acquires a Conversation-wide admission fence. A real service-plus-host regression holds interruption while another participant starts and replaces, verifies overlap rejection, and retains genuine Conversation fences and Stop generation/session ownership.

Any page-read HTTP 401/403 denial immediately unmounts the entire diagnostics surface and latches revocation despite stale public authorization metadata. Browser regressions cover receipt 401/403, status 403 and turn-failure 403 responses.

Successful per-participant Refresh upserts a missing participant while preserving other cached snapshots. A browser regression recovers two participants and their controls while collection reads remain unavailable, with zero lifecycle mutations.
delegatedReview.status: The follow-up independent review verified these three fixes, but requested changes for the late POST race recorded below.

followupReview.finding: A delayed acceptance POST failure could overwrite GET-confirmed completion with unconfirmed state and block the participant again.
followupReview.authorFix: Keep confirmed success/failure receipts immutable, ignore late POST outcomes after confirmation or superseding intent, avoid false mutation rollback, and retain 401/403 revocation before the stale-response guard.
followupReview.regressions: 18 owner tests cover successful/failed GET receipts followed by delayed transport/admission failure with unavailable reads, dismissed feedback preservation, superseding intents, late pending acceptance and late 401/403 denial.
followupReview.status: The final independent contextual review approved this correction, with one bounded non-blocking menu-lock finding.

checks: Working-tree fingerprint and whitespace checks passed

nonBlockingFinding.description: The transport-local submitting latch can keep eligible controls disabled until the acceptance POST settles, bounded by its default three-second timeout, despite an earlier exact terminal GET receipt.
nonBlockingFinding.disposition: Deferred and disclosed in the v0.0.19 release notes; no further behavior change was made.
